Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ A 甘味処 IS THE BEST DESSERT FORMAT IN JAPAN FOR BOTH DIETS AND ALMOST NOBODY KNOWS IT. The building blocks of this menu are 寒天 (agar, set from seaweed — not gelatine), あんこ (azuki beans and sugar), 白玉 (glutinous RICE flour dumplings), 黒蜜 (brown sugar syrup) and 赤えんどう (red peas). None of those is wheat and none is animal. So 豆かん at ¥830, あんみつ at ¥830, おしるこ and ぜんざい at ¥900 are, on their standard construction, both vegan and gluten-free — in a country where a coeliac normally cannot eat dessert at all. ⚠ WHAT BREAKS IT IS DAIRY, AND IT IS ALWAYS NAMED: クリーム, アイス and 抹茶クリーム are ice cream. The one wheat item is あんこトースト, which is bread. And おでん is the outlier on a sweet menu — a dashi broth, so fish, usually with wheat-starch-bulked fish cakes in it. ⚠ ONE THING TO ASK ANYWAY: some kanmi shops add ぎゅうひ (a soft mochi) or a wheat-flour wafer to an anmitsu, and the menu does not itemise what is in each bowl. The base is safe by construction; the garnish is the question.

A small French bistro built around seasonal produce and NATURAL WINE: 「当店は旬の食材を盛り込んだ料理とナチュラルワインを楽しんでいただくお店です」. No allergen statement is published. ⚠ A FRENCH BISTRO IS A BETTER PROSPECT FOR A COELIAC THAN ALMOST ANY JAPANESE FORMAT, FOR A STRUCTURAL REASON: the wheat sits in identifiable places — pastry, breadcrumb, the flour in a roux — rather than being dissolved through the seasoning the way soy sauce is in a Japanese kitchen. Here the mains are almost all ロティ, roasted, with a wine or mustard sauce; a roast is meat and heat. What has to be asked about is the SAUCE, because a French sauce is classically thickened with a beurre manié or built on a reduced stock, and neither is visible from a dish name. ⚠ TWO DISHES ARE WHEAT IN THEIR OWN NAMES: タブリエ・ド・サプール is トリッパのパン粉焼き — tripe in BREADCRUMB — and とうもろこしのフリット is a fritter, so battered. ⚠ AND FOR A VEGAN THIS IS CLOSED: every entrée and every main names a fish, a shellfish or a meat, the corn dish carries blue cheese and cream, and the bread that comes with a bistro meal is wheat. The natural-wine list is the one part a plant-eater can use, with the standing caveat that wine is routinely fined with egg white, casein or isinglass — natural wine being the style least likely to be.

tokyo_mametoku_asakusa_ten.price_note: Mametoku is a 豆菓子 maker trading since Meiji 2, not a restaurant, and the Asakusa branch is a takeaway confectionery counter three minutes from Kaminarimon. ⚠ THE SHOP PUBLISHES NO PRICE LIST FOR THE ASAKUSA COUNTER. Its own Asakusa page names two ASAKUSA-EXCLUSIVE lines — 「浅草あらかると」 and 「もんじゃ大豆」 — and describes them as 浅草店限定, but attaches no prices; the priced catalogue at mametoku.shop is the nationwide mail-order shop, whose range and pricing are not the counter’s, so those prices are deliberately NOT recorded here. ⚠ AND THE WHOLE CATEGORY IS A GLUTEN QUESTION THE SHOP NEVER ANSWERS: 豆菓子 means a bean under a coating, and the classic coating is a wheat-flour-and-sugar shell — the beans are the safe part, the shell is the unknown part. No allergen statement appears on any page. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02.

tokyo_matsutaro_shinjuku_kotak.price_note: No menu recoverable. 松太郎 is a Matsuya Foods ramen brand and the Shinjuku Kotakibashi-dori shop page carries only address, phone and hours (7:00–23:00, last order 30 minutes before close). The menu itself is published as a single JPEG image (260817_menu.jpg) with no text layer, so no dish name or price can be read from it. The brand also publishes a nutrition-and-allergen PDF, which was downloaded and run through pdftotext: the calorie, protein, fat, carbohydrate and salt columns extract cleanly but EVERY JAPANESE LABEL IS MISSING because the embedded fonts carry no ToUnicode mapping — numbers without the rows they belong to are unusable, so nothing from it is recorded. This is a finding, not a failure: an allergen chart exists and a person standing in the shop can read it, but it cannot be harvested from here. tokyo_chat_gatto_shagatto.price_note: The shop’s own FOOD page lists what it cooks but PUBLISHES NO PRICES AT ALL, closing with 「詳しくはお問い合わせください」 — ask us. Every item below is therefore recorded with the dish as the shop names it and no price. Chat Gatto is a Jimbocho wine bar built on ヴァンナチュール and produce shipped from EHIME: 大三島 organic vegetables, Imabari vegetables, Ehime-landed fish, and Ehime meats (イノシシ wild boar, 媛っこ地鶏, 七福豚). ⚠ THE FORMAT IS UNUSUALLY GOOD FOR A COELIAC AND UNUSUALLY BAD FOR A VEGAN. Good, because the cooking is roasting, grilling and steaming rather than sauce-building: 炭火焼き, ロースト, 白ワイン蒸し — wheat in an Italian kitchen sits in identifiable places (the pasta, the fritto batter) instead of being dissolved through the seasoning the way soy sauce is in a Japanese one. Bad, because the two dishes that are explicitly wheat are also the two most tempting — 新鮮魚介と野菜のフリットミスト is battered and 自家製パスタ is made in-house from wheat — and of the named dishes only the vegetable ones contain no animal. ⚠ AND THE WINE IS ITSELF A VEGAN QUESTION: natural wine is the style LEAST likely to be fined with egg white, casein or isinglass, but least likely is not none. No allergen statement is published. Tabelog not consulted: Cf-Mitigated: challenge (403) to this egress since 2026-09-02.

tokyo_suppon_denichi_minami_sh.price_note: Denichi is a 完全予約制 suppon (soft-shell turtle) kaiseki house at 渋谷区代々木2-15-12 クランツ南新宿1F, and it sells courses, not dishes — so the numbered plates below carry NO price of their own and the honest prices are the three lunch courses the shop lists on its own Gnavi page: 初まるコース ¥7,700, すっぽん革命コース ¥12,150 and すっぽん特選コース ¥16,650 (the last two shown after a 10% online-booking discount). The turtle is 佐賀県産はがくれすっぽん. ⚠ ONE GENUINELY GOOD GLUTEN FACT: the shop's own description of its すっぽんの唐揚げ says the pieces are dredged in くず粉 — kudzu starch, not wheat flour — which is rare enough in a Japanese fried dish to be worth knowing. It is then finished with ponzu, and ponzu is built on wheat soy sauce, so the dish as served is still not safe; ask whether the ponzu can be held back. ⚠ The 茶碗蒸し carries an あん sauce and shark fin, the 箸休め and 先付 are undescribed, and nothing here is vegan — every course is built on a three-hour turtle stock. The 手焼き最中 wafer that closes each course is a wheat monaka shell.

tokyo_thai_food_laboratory_tha.price_note: HONEST EMPTY. タイ料理研究所 渋谷店 (渋谷区桜丘町24-8 新南平台マンション1F) maintains its own Gnavi shop site, and both menu tabs on it are placeholders rather than menus: the コース tab reads only 「スタッフまでお問合せください」 and the ランチ tab only 「ランチメニューには生春巻きが付きます」— the lunch set comes with fresh spring rolls, which is the single concrete fact published anywhere reachable. No dish names, no prices. The shop is not on Tabelog-reachable egress this tick. For a Thai kitchen the standing gluten questions would be the fish sauce blend, the oyster and soy sauces in the stir-fries and the shared wok and fryer — none of which can be answered from what the shop publishes.

tokyo_sushi_iwase.price_note: HONEST EMPTY, but a informative one. 新宿 すし岩瀬 (西新宿3-4-1, near Tochomae) runs its own Gnavi shop site and its 夜のお品書き — the evening menu tab — contains exactly one line: 「おまかせのみ」. This is an omakase-only Edomae counter with no published à la carte and no published price; the chef decides and the figure is set on the night. That is a complete answer to 'what is the menu', not a gap in the research. For a coeliac the standing Edomae issues apply and cannot be resolved from anything published: the nikiri brushed onto the nigiri is wheat soy sauce, the tamago is usually bound with a dashi that carries soy, and the anago tsume is a soy-and-mirin reduction — ask the counter directly.

tokyo_maguro_to_shari.price_note: ⚠ THE MENU BELOW IS USER-SUBMITTED, NOT THE SHOP’S OWN BOARD, AND THAT IS THE FIRST THING TO KNOW ABOUT IT. Yahoo! Map heads this list ユーザー投稿のメニュー — items photographed and typed in by members of the public — and prints its own disclaimer, ※ 掲載時点の情報です。最新情報は店舗でご確認ください. Nothing here is dated. Some entries are visibly other diners’ shorthand rather than menu lines. It is recorded because it is the only itemised, priced list that exists for this shop on any page reachable from here, and because the dish names themselves are informative; treat every figure as approximate and every spelling as a diner’s. Hitosara was also read and confirms the shop itself: 渋谷区渋谷1-6-4 The Neat青山 1F, 03-6820-1052, open 11:00–21:00 every day of the week, average spend 1,000–1,999円 at both lunch and dinner — which brackets the donburi prices below and is the main reason to believe them. Hitosara carries no menu of its own. Instagram is the shop’s only listed channel and serves a login wall to this egress; Tabelog has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ WHAT A TUNA-BOWL COUNTER ACTUALLY MEANS FOR A COELIAC, AND IT IS BETTER NEWS THAN MOST OF THIS DATASET: raw tuna is fish and vinegared rice is rice, vinegar, sugar and salt — no wheat in either. The wheat at a kaisendon counter is almost entirely in the SOY SAUCE you pour on yourself, which means it is one of the few Japanese meals where the gluten is under your control rather than the kitchen’s. Bring tamari, or eat it with salt and wasabi. The two things that break that: the きつねうどん on this list, which is a wheat noodle in a soy-dashi broth and shares the kitchen, and the toppings — Japanese ikura is conventionally cured in soy (醤油漬け), and 納豆 arrives with a soy-and-dashi sachet. ⚠ NOTHING HERE IS VEGAN. This is a tuna shop; even the rice is a vehicle for it, and the only plant items on the list are toppings (avocado, tororo, nori) sold to go on top of fish.

items.en: The house bowl and the shop’s own coinage — “tuna and rice”, sold across a range because you build the size and the cut. Supervised, per the shop’s own publicity, by the Ginza sushi counter Hakkoku
items.note: 刺身と酢飯自体は小麦を含まないが、醤油は小麦。The tuna and the vinegared rice carry no wheat. The soy sauce does, and at this kind of counter it is normally poured by you at the table rather than pre-applied — ask whether the bowl arrives already sauced before you commit. Raw fish; not vegetarian in any version.

items.en: The top-grade version of the house bowl
items.note: Same construction, better cut of fish. Same soy-sauce question.

items.en: Medium-fatty and lean tuna together over rice, medium size
items.note: Two cuts of the same fish. Wheat risk is the soy only.

たたき＝叩いた赤身。Minced lean tuna. Note that a tataki mix is sometimes bound or seasoned in the kitchen rather than left plain, which would put the soy inside the bowl instead of on the table — worth asking.

items.ja: マグロ2色丼 いくらトッピング
items.en: Two-colour tuna bowl with salmon roe added
items.note: いくらは通常醤油漬け＝小麦。The ikura is the problem, not the tuna: Japanese salmon roe is conventionally cured in soy sauce and mirin, so it brings wheat into the bowl whether or not you pour any.

items.en: Mixed seafood bowl — assorted raw fish rather than tuna alone
items.note: A mixed bowl usually includes at least one item that has been marinated or glazed — anago, ikura, or a soy-cured cut — so it is a step less controllable than the plain tuna bowls. Ask what is on it.

items.en: Plain tuna bowl — the entry price
items.note: The simplest thing on the list and, for a coeliac, the most controllable: fish and rice with the soy on the side.

items.en: Kitsune udon — the odd item on a tuna counter’s list: wheat noodles in broth with a sheet of sweet simmered fried tofu
items.note: うどん＝小麦、つゆ＝鰹だし＋醤油、油揚げも醤油・味醂で煮る。Wheat in the noodle and wheat again in the soy of the broth; the broth is bonito dashi and the fried tofu is simmered in more soy. The tofu makes it look like the vegetarian option and it is not. Its presence also means there is a wheat-noodle pot in this kitchen.

items.en: Salmon roe, added to any bowl
items.note: 日本のいくらは醤油漬けが標準。Standard Japanese ikura is cured in soy sauce and mirin. Fish roe, so not vegetarian.

items.en: Sea urchin, added to any bowl
items.note: Uni is served raw and unseasoned, so it carries no wheat of its own — but board-grade uni is commonly treated with alum (ミョウバン) to hold its shape, which shops rarely declare. Not an allergen issue for gluten; worth knowing if additives matter to you.
Plain avocado — plant, no wheat of its own. Kept at ask for gluten only because it is being sliced in a kitchen that also runs a udon pot and pours soy.

items.en: Grated yam, added to any bowl
items.note: とろろは出汁と醤油で伸ばすのが一般的。Grated yam is a plant, but restaurant tororo is normally loosened with dashi and soy sauce rather than served neat — which would make it both a fish item and a wheat item. Ask whether it is seasoned.

items.en: Nori seaweed, added to any bowl
items.note: 焼海苔なら海藻のみ、味付海苔は醤油。Plain toasted nori is seaweed alone; seasoned nori is glazed with soy. Shops rarely say which.

items.en: Raw egg yolk, dropped on the bowl
items.note: A plain raw yolk carries no wheat. Egg, so not vegan.

items.en: Fermented soybeans, added to any bowl
items.note: 納豆自体は大豆と納豆菌のみだが、付属のタレは醤油＋かつおだし。The beans themselves are soybeans and culture and nothing else — genuinely wheat-free and genuinely plant. The sachet of tare that comes with every pack is soy sauce plus bonito extract, which is both a wheat and an animal ingredient. Ask for it without the tare and this is one of the cleanest items in the shop.

items.en: Size upgrades recorded by diners rather than dish names — a medium at 2,300円 and a large-medium at 2,000円
items.note: Recorded for completeness. These are portion steps on the tuna bowls above, not separate dishes, and they are exactly the kind of entry that shows this list was typed in by customers rather than copied from a board.

tokyo_nanjamonja.price_note: ⚠ TABELOG LISTS FOURTEEN ROWS FOR THIS SHOP AND TWELVE OF THEM ARE SECTION HEADINGS, NOT DISHES. "Monja", "Topping", "Teppan-yaki", "Salad", "Fried Food", "Rice Dishes", "Assorted Desserts" — these are the names of parts of a menu that was never transcribed, and they carry no prices. Only two rows are real, priced items. Rather than inflate this record to fourteen invented dishes, it holds the two that exist plus the structure, and says plainly that the rest of the carte is UNKNOWN. ⚠ THE DIETARY ANSWER, HOWEVER, DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE MISSING ITEMS, BECAUSE THIS IS A FLOUR-AND-GRIDDLE SHOP BY DEFINITION. お好み焼き is a batter of WHEAT FLOUR, egg and dashi; もんじゃ焼き is the same idea made deliberately runnier, and its batter is wheat flour loosened with dashi-thinned stock. Both are cooked on a shared 鉄板 that has had wheat batter on it all evening, and both are finished with お好みソース, a Worcester-style sauce that itself normally contains wheat. On top of that the standard garnishes are 青のり and かつおぶし — dried BONITO, i.e. fish flakes scattered over the finished dish as a matter of course. So: a coeliac cannot eat anything cooked on the griddle here, which is the entire point of the shop, and a vegetarian must ask for the dashi and the bonito to be left out of a dish where dashi is IN THE BATTER and cannot be removed. ⭐ TWO THINGS ABOUT THE SHOP ARE GENUINELY DISTINCTIVE AND BOTH ARE VISIBLE IN THE SECTION NAMES. First, it serves 関西風お好み焼き — KANSAI-STYLE, where the ingredients are mixed through the batter before cooking — in Shinjuku, which is Kanto and monja country; selling both side by side is the shop's proposition. Second, one section is 二郎系月島もんじゃ, "Jiro-style Tsukishima monja": ラーメン二郎 is a Tokyo ramen lineage famous for enormous piles of garlic, fat and bean sprouts, and applying that vocabulary to monja is a joke and a genuine menu category at once. Neither is conveyed by Tabelog's English, which flattens the second to "Jiro-style Monja". ⚠ THE 3,980円 COURSE IS THE ONE PRICE THAT MATTERS AND IT IS ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT AND ALL-YOU-CAN-DRINK FOR 150 MINUTES. For anyone with a restriction that is the worst possible format — the value is in eating widely off a shared griddle, which is exactly what cannot be done safely — and for everyone else it is the reason the recorded average spend is 3,000–3,999円. ON THE SHOP: 新宿3-7-5 一兆ビル, 3rd and 4th floors, 68 seats of which 66 are tatami, open 16:30–24:00 with food last orders at 23:00, and OPEN YEAR-ROUND with no fixed closing day.

items.en: 150-minute all-you-can-eat and all-you-can-drink course — the shop's headline offer
items.note: ⚠ 食べ放題は共用の鉄板で焼く＝小麦の完全な交差汚染。AN ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT GRIDDLE IS THE WORST FORMAT THERE IS FOR A RESTRICTED DINER. The contents are not published, but the shop is an okonomiyaki and monja house, so the course is built on WHEAT batter cooked on a communal hotplate, finished with wheat-containing sauce and BONITO flakes, and the batter itself is made with DASHI and EGG. There is no way to eat around it and no way to isolate a pan. Recorded because the price is real and the format is the single most important thing to know before booking.

items.en: Kansai-style okonomiyaki — cabbage and fillings mixed through the batter before it hits the griddle, rather than layered Hiroshima-style
items.section: 関西風お好み焼き・もんじゃ Kansai-style Okonomiyaki & Monja
items.note: ⚠ 生地＝小麦粉＋卵＋出汁。ソースにも小麦。THE BATTER IS THE DISH AND THE BATTER IS WHEAT — flour, EGG and DASHI (fish) mixed together, so there is no version without gluten and no version a vegetarian can order by removing a topping, because the stock is inside the batter. Finished with お好みソース (Worcester-style, normally contains WHEAT) and かつおぶし (dried BONITO). ⭐ The 関西風 label is the useful part: it tells you the fillings are folded through rather than stacked in layers, which is the Osaka method and not the Hiroshima one.
